notes: §1985:VI.6.15.4 GR2: 'If procedure-name-1 is not specified in format 1, an ALTER statement, referring to this GO TO statement, must be executed prior to the execution of this GO TO statement', a duty on the program whose observance the compiler must honour by transferring where the executed ALTER says. ControlFlowBinder.BindGoTo sends the target-less format to SetAlterBinder.AlterBindBareGoTo, which (after AlterEnsureScan's whole-program prepass of ALTER targets) binds a BoundGoToAlterable over the paragraph's _alter_ field with default -1; BindAlter binds each ALTER to that field and AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitAlter assigns the new destination, EmitFields declares the field per program instance, and EmitGoTo transfers to its current value. The 1985 edition reaches it because VersionConformancePass.VisitGoToStatement refuses the form only from 2002 (COBOL0811, probed) and accepts it at 85. A target-less GO TO executed before any ALTER, which the rule forbids and so leaves undefined, leaves the dispatcher loop and ends the run with no message (probed: exit 0). Probed at --std 85 beyond the witness: the same GO TO re-ALTERed three times, to paragraphs and to a section (first paragraph), follows the last executed ALTER each time. The witness exercises one ALTER then the GO TO.

next.reason: 1985: "If procedure-name-1 is not specified in format 1, an ALTER statement, referring to this GO TO statement, must be executed"; 2023: "GR-14.9.17.4-1: format 1 always names its target: "control is transferred to procedure-name-1"; no ALTER-dependent GO TO is stated". The 2023 GO TO rules cover format 1 only with procedure-name-1 given. The ALTER-set GO TO without a target is not carried, so the requirement is dropped.
